source_title: 2024 Report on Employer Firms: Findings from the 2023 Small Business Credit Survey
publisher_issuer: Federal Reserve Banks (Small Business Credit Survey, via fedsmallbusiness.org)
company_context: The Small Business Credit Survey (SBCS) is an annual survey of US small employer firms conducted by the Federal Reserve Banks. The 2024 Report on Employer Firms presents findings from the 2023 survey (fielded September-November 2023), describing base rates of financial and operational stress across the US small-business population.
business_type: US small businesses (employer firms) in aggregate across sectors; population-level base-rate dataset, not a single company
evidence_summary: The Federal Reserve's 2024 Report on Employer Firms documents that more than 9 in 10 firms experienced a financial or operational challenge in 2023. Rising costs of goods, services, and/or wages was the most common financial challenge, cited by 75% of firms; more than half cited paying operating expenses (56%) or uneven/uncertain cash flows (51%). For the first time since the 2021 survey, firms were more likely to report that revenues decreased rather than increased over the prior 12 months. Among firms denied some or all financing they applied for, 41% in 2024 (vs 22% in 2021) cited already having too much debt. These figures provide population-level base rates for cash-flow and working-capital stress among small businesses.

source_backed_metrics.revenue_trend: first time since 2021 survey that firms were more likely to report revenues decreased than increased over prior 12 months

outcome_evidence: Population-level survey result, not a single-firm outcome: documents prevalence of cash-flow and cost-driven financial challenges across US small employer firms in 2023.
source_limitations: Aggregate survey base rates, not a company-specific outcome; figures captured from fedsmallbusiness.org result snippets (PDF/landing page not fetched directly). Self-reported survey data with sampling/weighting caveats described in the full report.
directly_stated: More than 9 in 10 firms experienced a financial or operational challenge in 2023
56% cited paying operating expenses; 51% cited uneven cash flows
41% of denied firms in 2024 cited too much debt (vs 22% in 2021)
First time since 2021 that firms more likely reported revenues decreased than increased
inferred: Cash-flow/working-capital stress is a baseline condition for a large share of small businesses, not an anomaly
Elevated 'too much debt' denial reasons indicate tightening solvency headroom across the population
why_useful_for_opsiq: Provides empirical base rates for working_capital_stress and cash-flow problems across the small-business population. Useful for calibrating OpsIQ's priors so that a single firm's cash-flow stress is weighed against how common such stress is, preventing over-diagnosis, and for grounding BusinessConditionProfile thresholds.
